claim: Small angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) was used to determine the structure of the main immunoreactive region from LigB.
source: Here, we use a systematically designed series of multi-domain constructs in combination with small angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) to determine the structure of the main immunoreactive region from a major antigen from Leptospira interrogans, LigB.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states the methodology used to determine the structure.

claim: An anti-LigB monoclonal antibody library exhibits cell binding and bactericidal activity with extensive domain coverage.
source: An anti-LigB monoclonal antibody library exhibits cell binding and bactericidal activity with extensive domain coverage complementing the elongated architecture observed in the SAXS structure.
evidence: The abstract states the experimental findings regarding the mAb library.

claim: A chimeric immunoglobulin-like fold vaccine combining antigenic motifs greatly enhances leptospiral protection over vaccination with single parent domains.
source: Combining antigenic motifs in a single-domain chimeric immunoglobulin-like fold generated a vaccine that greatly enhances leptospiral protection over vaccination with single parent domains.
evidence: The abstract explicitly describes the vaccine performance results.

claim: The estimated worldwide burden of leptospirosis is over 1 million severe cases and ~60,000 deaths per year.
source: Because the estimated worldwide burden of leptospirosis is over 1 million severe cases and ~60,000 deaths per year, advances in recombinant leptospiral vaccines are desperately needed and are likely to benefit from a structure-based antigen design strategy (Picardeau, 2017; Costa et al., 2015).
evidence: The statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Currently available inactivated vaccines against leptospirosis are inadequate because of severe side-effects and lack of cross-protection among pathogenic Leptospira species.
source: Currently available inactivated vaccines against leptospirosis, the most common bacterial zoonosis (Picardeau, 2017), are inadequate because of the severe side-effects and lack of cross-protection among pathogenic Leptospira species (Grassmann et al., 2017; Adler, 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Leptospirosis is the most common bacterial zoonosis.
source: Currently available inactivated vaccines against leptospirosis, the most common bacterial zoonosis (Picardeau, 2017), are inadequate because of the severe side-effects and lack of cross-protection among pathogenic Leptospira species (Grassmann et al., 2017; Adler, 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: LigB is found in all pathogenic Leptospira genomes.
source: Lig proteins are present in only pathogenic species with LigB (but not LigA or LigC) being found in all pathogenic Leptospira genomes (McBride et al., 2009; Matsunaga et al., 2003)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: LigB's expression during host invasion suggests an important role in virulence.
source: LigB's expression during host invasion further suggests an important role in virulence (Lessa-Aquino et al., 2017; Choy et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature and represents an inference from expression data.

claim: LigB can bind multiple blood factors and extracellular matrix molecules (ECMs) to facilitate immune system evasion and tissue colonization.
source: To promote infection, LigB can bind multiple blood factors and extracellular matrix molecules (ECMs) to facilitate immune system evasion and tissue colonization (Choy, 2012; Vieira et al., 2014; Figueira et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: A hamster immunization study has suggested that LigB-derived vaccines have the potential to confer sterile immunity against leptospiral challenge.
source: Recently, a hamster immunization study has suggested that LigB-derived vaccines have the potential to confer sterile immunity against leptospiral challenge (Conrad et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Earlier LigB vaccine studies only confer partial protection.
source: The new study (Conrad et al., 2017) is inconsistent with earlier LigB vaccine studies which only confer partial protection (Yan et al., 2009; Silva et al., 2007)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: LigB is attached to the leptospiral outer surface by a short N-terminal anchor, followed by twelve consecutive Ig-like domains, and flanked at its C-terminus by an additional non-Ig-like domain.
source: LigB is attached to the leptospiral outer surface by a short N-terminal anchor, which is followed by a stretch of twelve consecutive Ig-like domains, and flanked at its C-terminus by an additional non-Ig-like domain (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by reference to a figure showing the protein structure.

claim: All eight possible 5-domain protein constructs (LigB1-5 to LigB8-12) were analyzed with SAXS.
source: All eight possible 5-domain protein constructs (LigB1-5 to LigB8-12) were analyzed with SAXS (Figure 1; Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The manuscript describes the experimental approach and references supporting figures.

claim: Guinier fits and Porod analysis suggested minimal aggregation for all but LigB5-9.
source: Guinier fits and Porod analysis suggested minimal aggregation for all but LigB5-9 (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B and Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is based on specific analytical methods applied to the SAXS data.

claim: The expected length of a fully extended arrangement of five folded LigB Ig-like domains is only slightly longer than the pair distance for most of the eight 5-domain proteins.
source: The expected length of a fully extended arrangement of five folded LigB Ig-like domains is only slightly longer than the pair distance for most of the eight 5-domain proteins and their corresponding envelopes (Figure 1B; Figure 1—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: The claim compares theoretical and experimental measurements from SAXS data.

claim: LigB5-9 has an atomic pair distance that exceeds what is possible for a folded 5-domain monomer.
source: LigB5-9 has an atomic pair distance that exceeds what is possible for a folded 5-domain monomer (in agreement with aggregation indicated by the difference between experimental and predicted molecular weights, Figure 1—source data 1) and was excluded from the final model.
evidence: The claim is based on SAXS measurements and molecular weight analysis.

claim: The first six structures (LigB1-5 to LigB6-10) have a high degree of uniqueness with ambiguity scores of 0.3 or lower.
source: Ambiguity assessment using the AMBIMETER program (Petoukhov and Svergun, 2015) shows that the first six structures (LigB1-5 to LigB6-10) have a high degree of uniqueness with ambiguity scores of 0.3 or lower.
evidence: The claim is based on computational analysis of SAXS data using a specific program.

claim: The last two structures (LigB7-11 and LigB8-12) have ambiguity scores of 1.7 and 1.4 respectively, which indicates the potential for shape ambiguity.
source: The last two structures (LigB7-11 and LigB8-12) have scores of 1.7 and 1.4 respectively, which indicates the potential for shape ambiguity.
evidence: The claim is based on computational analysis of SAXS data.

claim: The SAXS-derived structure of LigB1-12 is only 16% shorter than a fully extended model structure of twelve folded domains.
source: Overall the LigB1-12 structure is only 16% shorter than a fully extended model structure of twelve folded domains.
evidence: The claim compares the experimental structure to a theoretical model.

claim: Two purified LigB truncations, LigB1-7 and LigB7-12, were used to generate two sets of hybridoma cell lines for mAb production: library C (24 mAbs) and library V (36 mAbs).
source: To explore the exposure of the LigB Ig-like domain region to a host immune response, two purified LigB truncations, LigB1-7 and LigB7-12 (Figure 2A), were used to generate two sets of hybridoma cell lines for mAb production: library C (24 mAbs) and library V (36 mAbs), respectively.
evidence: The manuscript describes the experimental approach for generating mAbs.

claim: A threshold level for mAb binding efficiency was set to OD630 = 1.0.
source: Based on the distribution of antigen binding efficiencies, a threshold level was set to OD630 = 1.0 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The manuscript describes the experimental criteria for selecting mAbs.

claim: Library C mAbs were generally able to bind tighter to the LigB antigen than library V mAbs based on KD values.
source: Based on KD values, library C mAbs were generally able to bind tighter to the LigB antigen than library V mAbs.
evidence: The claim is based on dissociation constant measurements from ELISA experiments.

claim: Several library C mAbs (C5, C6, C7) exhibit sub-micromolar KD values.
source: Several library C mAbs (C5, C6, C7) exhibit sub-micromolar KD values while only one library V mAb (V10) was able to bind in the sub-micromolar range.
evidence: The claim is based on dissociation constant measurements from ELISA experiments.

claim: Only one library V mAb (V10) was able to bind in the sub-micromolar range.
source: Several library C mAbs (C5, C6, C7) exhibit sub-micromolar KD values while only one library V mAb (V10) was able to bind in the sub-micromolar range.
evidence: The claim is based on dissociation constant measurements from ELISA experiments.

claim: For the LigB1-7 antigen-derived library, immunoreactivity of mAbs was weighted towards LigB1-2 and LigB4-5 regions.
source: For the LigB1-7 antigen-derived library, immunoreactivity of mAbs was weighted towards LigB1-2 and LigB4-5 regions, while for the LigB7-12 antigen-derived library, mAbs were preferentially generated against LigB7-8 and LigB10-11 regions.
evidence: The claim is based on epitope mapping experiments using ELISA.

claim: For the LigB7-12 antigen-derived library, mAbs were preferentially generated against LigB7-8 and LigB10-11 regions.
source: For the LigB1-7 antigen-derived library, immunoreactivity of mAbs was weighted towards LigB1-2 and LigB4-5 regions, while for the LigB7-12 antigen-derived library, mAbs were preferentially generated against LigB7-8 and LigB10-11 regions.
evidence: The claim is based on epitope mapping experiments using ELISA.

claim: Only 3 of 10 double domains (LigB3-4, LigB6-7, and LigB8-9) and 2 of 12 single domains (LigB3 and LigB11) lack immunogenicity for the set of tested mAbs.
source: Only 3 of 10 double domains, LigB3-4, LigB6-7, and LigB8-9, and 2 of 12 single domains, LigB3 and LigB11, lack immunogenicity for the set of tested mAbs.
evidence: The claim is based on epitope mapping experiments using ELISA.

claim: All tested anti-LigB mAbs produced a fluorescence signal count over three-fold higher than the PBS control and over two-fold higher than the poorly binding mAb controls (C22 and V33).
source: A total of seven library C mAbs and six library V mAbs were measured for Leptospira surface binding character and all produced a fluorescence signal count over three-fold higher than the PBS control and over two-fold higher than the poorly binding mAb controls (C22 and V33) (Figure 4—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: The claim is based on flow cytometry measurements.

claim: The flow cytometry data supports the presence of mAb-accessible Lig protein Ig-like domains on the surface of Leptospira cells.
source: The flow cytometry data supports the presence of mAb-accessible Lig protein Ig-like domains on the surface of Leptospira cells.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of flow cytometry data.

claim: The PBS only (negative control) condition was unable to effectively kill the live Leptospira cells leaving an 84% survival rate at 120 min post treatment.
source: The PBS only (negative control) condition was unable to effectively kill the live Leptospira cells leaving an 84% survival rate at 120 min post treatment (Figure 5A).
evidence: The claim is based on bactericidal assay measurements.

claim: The hamster-derived polyclonal antibody (pAb) treatment of Leptospira cells led to an enhancement of bactericidal activity with only 63% survival at 120 min post treatment.
source: The hamster-derived polyclonal antibody (pAb) treatment of Leptospira cells led to an enhancement of bactericidal activity with only 63% survival at 120 min post treatment.
evidence: The claim is based on bactericidal assay measurements.

claim: Leptospira incubated with C5 or V10 mAbs showed only a 2% to 3% survival rate (a >20 fold improvement over pAb-incubated spirochetes p<0.05).
source: Leptospira incubated with C5 or V10 mAbs showed only a 2% to 3% survival rate (a >20 fold improvement over pAb-incubated spirochetes p<0.05) (Figure 5A).
evidence: The claim is based on bactericidal assay measurements with statistical analysis.

claim: All anti-LigB mAbs were able to eliminate >50% of Leptospira between 40 and 85 min with the exception of mAb C23.
source: All anti-LigB mAbs were able to eliminate >50% of Leptospira between 40 and 85 min with the exception of mAb C23 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is based on time-dependent bactericidal assay measurements.

claim: All of the LigB-specific mAbs were able to effectively decrease the number of metabolically active Leptospira cells to less than 50% with a dose value (LD50) between 10 and 30 μg/ml.
source: All of the LigB-specific mAbs were able to effectively decrease the number of metabolically active Leptospira cells to less than 50% with a dose value (LD50) between 10 and 30 μg/ml (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is based on dose-dependent bactericidal assay measurements.

claim: The LigB proteins from L. interrogans serovar Manilae and L. interrogans serovar Pomona share 96% identity.
source: Note that the LigB proteins from L. interrogans serovar Manilae and L. interrogans serovar Pomona share 96% identity suggesting that the bactericidal properties provided by the LigB (Pomona) mAb library using these two serovars would be similar.
evidence: The claim is based on sequence comparison.

claim: A trendline for KD vs. LD50 scatter plots using all data yields a correlation with R²=0.508.
source: A trendline for KD vs. LD50 scatter plots using all data and excluding the two statistically-determined outliers (Figure 5D; Figure 5—figure supplement 2) yields correlations with R²=0.508 and R²=0.773, respectively.
evidence: The claim is based on statistical analysis of experimental data.

claim: A trendline for KD vs. LD50 scatter plots excluding the two statistically-determined outliers yields a correlation with R²=0.773.
source: A trendline for KD vs. LD50 scatter plots using all data and excluding the two statistically-determined outliers (Figure 5D; Figure 5—figure supplement 2) yields correlations with R²=0.508 and R²=0.773, respectively.
evidence: The claim is based on statistical analysis of experimental data.

claim: When plotted against LD50, FACS-derived cell binding values fit to a trendline with an R²=0.312.
source: When plotted against LD50, FACS-derived cell binding values fit to a trendline with an R²=0.312 and the single outlier-adjusted trendline of with an R²=0.466 (Figure 5E; Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is based on statistical analysis of experimental data.

claim: The single outlier-adjusted trendline for FACS cell binding vs. LD50 has an R²=0.466.
source: When plotted against LD50, FACS-derived cell binding values fit to a trendline with an R²=0.312 and the single outlier-adjusted trendline of with an R²=0.466 (Figure 5E; Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is based on statistical analysis of experimental data.

claim: C12 is the only library C mAb that can also bind to LigB7-12.
source: Further, an additional ELISA assay found that C12 is the only library C mAb that can also bind to LigB7-12 (Figure 5—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is based on ELISA binding experiments.

claim: Two LigB7-specific mAbs (V12 and V34), two LigB10-specific mAbs (V1 and V10), and one LigB12-specific mAb (V2) could bind only to the N-terminal β-strands A-C from their respective interacting domains.
source: Two LigB7-specific mAbs (V12 and V34), two LigB10-specific mAbs (V1 and V10), and one LigB12-specific mAb (V2) could bind only to the N-terminal β-strands A-C from their respective interacting domains.
evidence: The claim is based on chimera binding experiments.

claim: The LigB5-specific mAb C5 and LigB7-specfic mAb V3 interacted with proteins that contained β-strands C′-F from LigB5 and LigB7, respectively.
source: The LigB5-specific mAb C5 and LigB7-specfic mAb V3 interacted with proteins that contained β-strands C′-F from LigB5 and LigB7, respectively.
evidence: The claim is based on chimera binding experiments.

claim: mAb V11 and mAb C6 required both the β-strands C′-F and the terminal β-strands G-G′ from LigB12 and LigB5, respectively.
source: Unique to the LigB5/LigB12 mAb set, mAb V11 and mAb C6 required both the β-strands C′-F and the terminal β-strands G-G′ from LigB12 and LigB5, respectively.
evidence: The claim is based on chimera binding experiments.

claim: The mAb binding patterns demonstrate that the surface contribution of both β-strands A-C and β-strands C′-F (or C′-G′) can provide distinct epitopes for direct mAb targeting.
source: The mAb binding patterns demonstrate that the surface contribution of both β-strands A-C and β-strands C′-F (or C′-G′) can provide distinct epitopes for direct mAb targeting.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the chimera binding experiments.

claim: LigB10-B7-B7 was similar to wild-type LigB7 and LigB10 in protein expression levels and in overall secondary structure.
source: Additionally, LigB10-B7-B7 was similar to wild-type LigB7 and LigB10 in protein expression levels and in overall secondary structure (circular dichroism analysis, Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is based on protein expression and circular dichroism measurements.

claim: On day 8, the leptospiral challenge was lethal for five of six hamsters inoculated with PBS group.
source: On day 8, the leptospiral challenge was lethal for five of six hamsters inoculated with PBS group, three of five hamsters inoculated with wild-type LigB7, and four of five hamsters inoculated with wild-type LigB10.
evidence: The claim is based on hamster challenge experiments.

claim: On day 8, the leptospiral challenge was lethal for three of five hamsters inoculated with wild-type LigB7.
source: On day 8, the leptospiral challenge was lethal for five of six hamsters inoculated with PBS group, three of five hamsters inoculated with wild-type LigB7, and four of five hamsters inoculated with wild-type LigB10.
evidence: The claim is based on hamster challenge experiments.

claim: On day 8, the leptospiral challenge was lethal for four of five hamsters inoculated with wild-type LigB10.
source: On day 8, the leptospiral challenge was lethal for five of six hamsters inoculated with PBS group, three of five hamsters inoculated with wild-type LigB7, and four of five hamsters inoculated with wild-type LigB10.
evidence: The claim is based on hamster challenge experiments.

claim: By day 10, all of the wild-type LigB7 and LigB10 immunized hamsters had either died or were euthanized due to severe clinical signs.
source: By day 10, all of the wild-type LigB7 and LigB10 immunized hamsters had either died or were euthanized due to severe clinical signs.
evidence: The claim is based on hamster challenge experiments.

claim: All five of the hamsters that had been inoculated with LigB10-B7-B7 and subsequently challenged with Leptospira survived until the end of the experiment (day 21 post infection).
source: In contrast, all five of the hamsters that had been inoculated with LigB10-B7-B7 and subsequently challenged with Leptospira survived until the end of the experiment (day 21 post infection).
evidence: The claim is based on hamster challenge experiments.

claim: The survival rate of the LigB10-B7-B7 group is significantly higher (100%) than either control group (17%) or individual wild-type domain groups (0%) (p<0.05).
source: The survival rate of the LigB10-B7-B7 group is significantly higher (100%) than either control group (17%) or individual wild-type domain groups (0%) (p<0.05).
evidence: The claim is based on hamster challenge experiments with statistical analysis.

claim: The hamster group that received immunizations containing recombinant chimeric protein, LigB10-B7-B7, exhibited a significant reduction in leptospiral burden when compared to bacterial loads from wild-type LigB7 or LigB10 immunized hamsters.
source: The hamster group that received immunizations containing recombinant chimeric protein, LigB10-B7-B7, exhibited a significant reduction in leptospiral burden when compared to bacterial loads from wild-type LigB7 or LigB10 immunized hamsters.
evidence: The claim is based on RT-qPCR measurements of bacterial loads in hamster tissues.

claim: All hamsters immunized with chimeric LigB10-B7-B7 presented no visible macroscopic/microscopic lesions in livers, kidneys or lungs.
source: In contrast, all hamsters immunized with chimeric LigB10-B7-B7 presented no visible macroscopic/microscopic lesions in livers, kidneys or lungs (Figure 7F–H).
evidence: The claim is based on histopathological examination of hamster tissues.

claim: Vaccines containing the chimeric antigen provide superior protection and potentially sterilizing immunity for the animals from leptospiral infection.
source: In agreement with high survival rate of LigB10-B7-B7 immunized hamsters, vaccines containing the chimeric antigen provide superior protection and potentially sterilizing immunity for the animals from leptospiral infection.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the hamster challenge and tissue analysis data.

claim: Lig proteins contribute to pathogenesis by acting as both surface adhesins to mediate attachment to host extracellular matrix (ECM) molecules and recruiters of complement regulators to evade attack by the host's innate immune system.
source: Lig proteins contribute to pathogenesis by acting as both surface adhesins to mediate attachment to host extracellular matrix (ECM) molecules (Lin et al., 2009a; Vieira et al., 2014; Figueira et al., 2011) and recruiters of complement regulators to evade attack by the host's innate immune system (Breda et al., 2015; Choy et al., 2007; Hsieh et al., 2016; Castiblanco-Valencia et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: The domain arrangement of the LigB1-12 Ig-like domain region was determined using low resolution SAXS structures.
source: The domain arrangement of the LigB1-12 Ig-like domain region was determined using low resolution SAXS structures.
evidence: The manuscript describes the methodology used.

claim: The SAXS-derived LigB1-12 structure provides a visual depiction that complements the more therapeutically applicable information from mAb accessibility.
source: The SAXS-derived LigB1-12 structure provides a visual depiction that complements the more therapeutically applicable information from mAb accessibility.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the combined structural and immunological data.

claim: The full LigB structure is the first example of using a sliding window of medium length, 5-domain constructs to generate a much longer 12-domain structure.
source: While previous SAXS studies have generated composite multi-domain structures (Jeffries et al., 2011; Morgan et al., 2012), the full LigB structure is the first example of using a sliding window of medium length, 5-domain constructs to generate a much longer 12-domain structure.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous work and describes the novelty of the approach.

claim: The sequence of domains LigB1-6 is identical to LigA domains 1–6 so the SAXS structure provides a partial structure of the LigA Ig-like domain region.
source: The sequence of domains LigB1-6 is identical to LigA domains 1–6 so the SAXS structure provides a partial structure of the LigA Ig-like domain region.
evidence: The claim is based on sequence comparison and structural inference.

claim: Ig-like domains are found in a variety of prokayotic and eukaryotic extracellular proteins and readily fold to their native structure.
source: Ig-like domains are found in a variety of prokayotic and eukaryotic extracellular proteins and readily fold to their native structure (Bodelón et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Based on the high resolution LigB12 structure, each of the three chimeric segments encompassed a 900 to 2000 Å2 surface and could potentially make a full conformational epitope.
source: Based on the high resolution LigB12 structure, each of the three chimeric segments encompassed a 900 to 2000 Å2 surface and could potentially make a full conformational epitope (Ptak et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is based on structural analysis and is supported by a citation.

claim: The single domain LigB10-B7-B7 provides better protection to hamsters than two longer constructs, LigB7-12 (which provided poor protection) and LigB1-7 (which provided good protection).
source: Interestingly, the single domain LigB10-B7-B7 provides better protection to hamsters than two longer constructs, LigB7-12 (which provided poor protection) and LigB1-7 (which provided good protection) (Yan et al., 2009; Conrad et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is based on hamster challenge experiments and is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The 5-domain length contains four domain-domain linkers, making the 5-domain structure optimal to define the relative angle of two neighboring domain-domain joints with one additional joint on each end.
source: Because the 5-domain length contains four domain-domain linkers, the 5-domain structure proved to be optimal to define the relative angle of two neighboring domain-domain joints with one additional joint on each end (See Materials and methods for rationale; Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim explains the rationale for the experimental design.

claim: The advantage of using a sliding window is that the high level of redundancy within the 5-domain structures allows for an increased accuracy in orienting and positioning the segments relative to each other.
source: The advantage of using a sliding window is that the high level of redundancy within the 5-domain structures allows for an increased accuracy in orienting and positioning the segments relative to each other.
evidence: The claim explains the methodological advantage of the approach.

claim: A significant degree of bending is present between the first three domains.
source: A significant degree of bending is present between the first three domains.
evidence: The claim is based on analysis of SAXS structures.

claim: The stretch of domains between LigB3-6 is particularly straight.
source: The stretch of domains between LigB3-6 is particularly straight.
evidence: The claim is based on analysis of SAXS structures.

claim: Slight bending in the angle between domains in the final five domain stretch produces a gentle spiral shape.
source: Slight bending in the angle between domains in the final five domain stretch produces a gentle spiral shape.
evidence: The claim is based on analysis of SAXS structures.

claim: The SAXS-derived structure of LigB1-12 demonstrates that most of the individual Ig-like domains exhibit a high degree of exposed surface area and suggests a high degree of accessibility to host interactions.
source: The SAXS-derived structure of LigB1-12 demonstrates that most of the individual Ig-like domains exhibit a high degree of exposed surface area and suggests a high degree of accessibility to host interactions.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the SAXS structure.

claim: The extensive exposed surface area is a consequence of the unexpected rigid, rod-like structure, with several well-defined kinks.
source: The extensive exposed surface area is a consequence of the unexpected rigid, rod-like structure, with several well-defined kinks.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the SAXS structure.

claim: The ability of the anti-LigB mAbs to kill Leptospira in the presence of complement is consistent with their capability in binding to LigB protein in pathogenic Leptospira.
source: The ability of the anti-LigB mAbs to kill Leptospira in the presence of complement is consistent with their capability in binding to LigB protein in pathogenic Leptospira.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the combined binding and bactericidal data.

claim: The broad mAb accessibility of LigB Ig-like domains supports the extended organization of the LigB1-12 SAXS structure.
source: The broad mAb accessibility of LigB Ig-like domains supports the extended organization of the LigB1-12 SAXS structure.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the combined structural and immunological data.

claim: C12 displays some specificity for the straightest segment (LigB4-6), it can bind to two single domains (LigB4 and LigB6) as well as a double domain in the segment LigB1-3.
source: While C12 displays some specificity for the straightest segment (LigB4-6), it can bind to two single domains (LigB4 and LigB6) as well as a double domain in the segment LigB1-3.
evidence: The claim is based on epitope mapping experiments.

claim: The ability of C12 to bind to multiple Ig-like domains covering a large range of the Ig-like domain regions suggests a reason for the increased bactericidal activity relative to C12's binding affinity.
source: The ability of C12 to bind to multiple Ig-like domains covering a large range of the Ig-like domain regions suggests a reason for the increased bactericidal activity relative to C12's binding affinity.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the epitope mapping and bactericidal data.

claim: C23 binds to LigB2-3, which exhibit the sharpest interdomain bend.
source: The only outlier with bactericidal activity below expected is C23 which binds to LigB2-3. These domain neighbors exhibit the sharpest interdomain bend suggesting that steric limitations can differentially effect LigB binding and bactericidal activity.
evidence: The claim is based on epitope mapping and structural analysis.

claim: Steric limitations can differentially effect LigB binding and bactericidal activity.
source: These domain neighbors exhibit the sharpest interdomain bend suggesting that steric limitations can differentially effect LigB binding and bactericidal activity.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the structural and functional data.

claim: The kinked structure of C23's target domain may decrease the rate for C23 to initiate bacterial killing relative to its KD.
source: Indeed, the kinked structure of C23's target domain may decrease the rate for C23 to initiate bacterial killing relative to its KD (Figure 5—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The claim is a speculative interpretation of the structural and functional data.

claim: The link between antigen binding and bactericidal activity complements the highly accessible extended structure of LigB with highly accessible regions having the potential to yield high bactericidal mAbs.
source: Overall, the link between antigen binding and bactericidal activity complements the highly accessible extended structure of LigB with highly accessible regions having the potential to yield high bactericidal mAbs.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the combined structural and functional data.

claim: The chimera LigB10-B7-B7 (β-strands A-C: B10 and β-strands C′-F and G-G′: B7) was chosen as the best candidate for animal studies because the chimeric domain possesses the ability to bind highly bactericidal mAbs specific to each parent domain.
source: The chimera LigB10-B7-B7 (β-strands A-C: B10 and β-strands C′-F and G-G′: B7) was chosen as the best candidate for animal studies because the chimeric domain possesses the ability to bind highly bactericidal mAbs specific to each parent domain (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim explains the rationale for selecting the chimera for vaccine studies.

claim: LigB10-B7-B7 immunization led to an increase in post-booster secondary response for IgG but not IgM antibodies implying the generation of a typical immune memory response.
source: LigB10-B7-B7 immunization led to an increase in post-booster secondary response for IgG but not IgM antibodies implying the generation of a typical immune memory response (Figure 7—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is based on serological analysis and represents an interpretation of the immune response.

claim: Exposure of epitopes in single domain antigens which would otherwise be blocked by host factors (i.e., ECM or serum proteins) in multi-domain constructs may enhance the efficiency.
source: Exposure of epitopes in single domain antigens which would otherwise be blocked by host factors (Beernink et al., 2011) (i.e., ECM or serum proteins [Lin et al., 2009a; Breda et al., 2015; Hsieh et al., 2016]) in multi-domain constructs may enhance the efficiency.
evidence: The claim is a speculative interpretation supported by citations to published literature.

claim: The 8-domain long construct (LigB5-12) failed to generate envelopes with distinct domain regions representative of possible 8-domain structures.
source: The 8-domain long construct (LigB5-12) failed to generate envelopes with distinct domain regions representative of possible 8-domain structures.

claim: High average normalized spatial discrepancy (NSD) values for a reconstruction indicate increased variability among the trial models used to build the final envelope.
